intro.text: Acuity Inc. (referred to herein as “we,” “our,” “us,” the “Company,” or similar references) is a market-leading industrial technology company. We use technology to solve problems in spaces, light, and more things to come. Through our two business segments, Acuity Brands Lighting (“ABL”) and Acuity Intelligent Spaces (“AIS”), we design, manufacture, and bring to market products and services that make a valuable difference in people’s lives. We achieve growth through the development of innovative new products and services, including lighting, lighting controls, building management solutions, and an audio, video, and control platform. We focus on customer outcomes and drive growth and productivity to increase market share and deliver superior returns. We look to aggressively deploy capital to grow the business and to enter attractive new verticals.

Cash flows from operations decreased as payments for acquisition-related costs, higher interest, and increased purchases of inventory were partially offset by the timing of collections from customers.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text: Net sales of $4.35 billion for the year ended August 31, 2025 increased by $504.6 million, or 13.1%, compared with the prior-year period due primarily to increases in sales in both our AIS and ABL segments. The increase in our AIS segment was driven by the acquisition of QSC, which contributed $428.6 million in sales, as well higher net sales of our Atrius and Distech products. Additionally, net sales increased in our ABL segment due primarily to higher net sales within the independent sales and direct sales networks, partially offset by lower net sales within the corporate accounts and retail channels.

gp.heading: Gross Profit
gp.text:
Gross profit for the year ended August 31, 2026 increased $272.2 million, or 13.1%, to $2.35 billion compared with $2.08 billion for the prior year. This increase was due primarily to contributions from the QSC acquisition as well as the fall through of higher net sales of our Distech products. Additionally, in fiscal 2026 we received $51.3 million in refunds from U.S. Customs for tariffs previously paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (“IEEPA”), and in fiscal 2025 we recorded $29.6 million in pre-tax nonrecurring acquisition date fair value adjustments to inventory related to the acquisition of QSC. These increases were partially offset by the fall through of lower net sales within the ABL segment.

Please refer to the Commitments and Contingencies footnote of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements within this Annual Report on Form 10-K for further details regarding tariff refunds.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense, net
nonop.text: We reported net interest expense of $25.6 million and $22.0 million for the years ended August 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. Net interest expense increased year over year as lower interest income was partially offset by a decline in interest expense. These changes reflect both lower outstanding cash balances as well as lower outstanding borrowings during fiscal 2026.

tax.heading: Income Taxes and Net Income
tax.text:
Our effective income tax rate was 21.9% and 20.7% for the years ended August 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. This year-over-year increase was due primarily to a one-time $8.2 million tax benefit recorded in fiscal 2025 related to the expiration of the statute of limitations on tax reserves for uncertain tax positions. Further details regarding income taxes are included in the Income Taxes footnote of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements .

Net income for fiscal 2026 increased $134.7 million, or 34.0%, to $531.3 million from $396.6 million reported for the prior year. This increase was due primarily to higher operating profit and lower net miscellaneous expense, partially offset by higher income tax expense associated with the increase in profit and higher net interest expense.

Diluted earnings per share for fiscal 2026 was $17.05 compared with $12.53 for the prior-year period, an increase of $4.52, or 36.1%. This increase reflects higher net income as well as lower outstanding diluted shares.

net.heading: Income Taxes and Net Income
net.text:
Our effective income tax rate was 21.9% and 20.7% for the years ended August 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. This year-over-year increase was due primarily to a one-time $8.2 million tax benefit recorded in fiscal 2025 related to the expiration of the statute of limitations on tax reserves for uncertain tax positions. Further details regarding income taxes are included in the Income Taxes footnote of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements .

Net income for fiscal 2026 increased $134.7 million, or 34.0%, to $531.3 million from $396.6 million reported for the prior year. This increase was due primarily to higher operating profit and lower net miscellaneous expense, partially offset by higher income tax expense associated with the increase in profit and higher net interest expense.

Diluted earnings per share for fiscal 2026 was $17.05 compared with $12.53 for the prior-year period, an increase of $4.52, or 36.1%. This increase reflects higher net income as well as lower outstanding diluted shares.

ocf.text: We generated $825.6 million of cash flows from operating activities during fiscal 2026 compared with $601.4 million in the prior-year period, an increase of $224.2 million. Cash flows from operations increased due primarily to higher profit, including $51.3 million of received tariff refunds, and lower income tax payments.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text: Net sales of $4.64 billion for the year ended August 31, 2026 increased by $296.2 million, or 6.8%, compared with the prior year due primarily to higher sales in our AIS segment, partially offset by lower sales in our ABL segment. The increase in our AIS segment was driven by the acquisition of QSC, as well as higher net sales of our Distech products.

lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During fiscal 2026, net sales initiated outside of the U.S. represented approximately 13% of total net sales.

Although no individual customer exceeded 10% of net sales during fiscal 2026, 2025, or 2024, the loss of or a substantial decrease in the volume of purchases by certain larger customers could harm our business in a meaningful manner.
No single customer accounted for more than 10% of receivables at August 31, 2026 or August 31, 2025.
No single customer accounted for more than 10% of net sales in fiscal 2026, 2025, or 2024.

Sales of lighting, lighting controls, building management solutions, and audio, video, and control solutions, excluding services accounted for approximately 99 % of total consolidated net sales in fiscal 2026, 2025, and 2024.
We purchase most raw materials and other components on the open market and rely on third parties to provide certain finished goods.
We rely on patent, copyright, trade secret, and trademark laws as well as agreements, restrictive covenants, and internal processes and controls to protect these proprietary rights.

The success of new product and solution introductions depends on a number of factors, including, but not limited to, timely and successful product development, product quality, market acceptance, including entrance into new verticals, and our ability to manage the risks associated with product life cycles.

Future disruptions in the supply chain, shortages, import and export bans, sanctions, or tariffs imposed by the U.S. or foreign governments have affected or could continue to affect our ability to procure components for our products on a timely basis, or at all, or could require us to commit to increased purchases or longer term guaranteed supply agreements, secure new suppliers, rely on relatively high-cost spot market purchases, and provide longer lead times to secure critical components.

However, there are a limited number of suppliers for certain components and certain purchased finished goods, which on a limited basis have resulted in and may result in sole-source supplier situations.

While we maintain positive, and in many cases long-term, relationships with these channel partners, the sudden or unplanned loss of a number of these channel partners or a substantial decrease in the volume of purchases from a major channel partner or a group of channel partners could adversely affect our business.

For example, a customer may depend on integral information from, or functionality of, our technology to support that customer’s other systems, such that a failure of our technology could impact those systems, including by loss or destruction of data.
We rely upon the knowledge and experience of employees involved in functions throughout the organization that require technical expertise and knowledge of the industry.
Our operations, as well as those of key vendors, are therefore subject to regulatory, economic, political, military, and other events in countries where these operations are located.
